verdict: READY TO MERGE - 9 of 9 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: The updated `skill` description (line 45) matches the code: forked rows go through unclaimedDispatch with SKILL set to the skill name, so the plugin-prefix strip and pattern fallback apply the same way as for a header value.
The `from agent-watcher 0.8.0 on` claim agrees with the agent-watcher plugin.json version at the PR head, and the harness plugin version is bumped alongside the schema edit.
The change is description-only: pattern, required list and additionalProperties are untouched, so existing rows keep validating.

The forked-skill tests run end to end through the engine, with fake files, clock, agent list and shell beneath the plugin. Nothing under test is stubbed, and the row assertions pin every usage field (tokens 100 from loop usage, context_tokens 500 from the last request, requests 2, tool_uses 1, model family from the loop's usage).
The resumed-fork test checks the probe reset at loop end (tracker.ts:352) by requiring two distinct run ids across two runs of turns on one loop id.

The negative cases cover a loop the list does not name, a description that is not a single `/<skill>` token, and a project with no harness config, where `asked.calls === 0` proves the lookup is skipped and not just that no row is written.

The `_prompt_block` change in test_dispatch_skill_headers.py (allow indented closing fences, strip each line) is the smallest edit that lets the list-indented roast-my-code prompt block parse. The added `marker` parameter defaults to the old 'Project root:', so the existing skill checks behave as before.
The new roast-my-code test names both `SKILL.md` and the `roast-my-code` anchor in its source, so tools/select_tests.py runs it when that skill's prose changes.
Fork handling reuses unclaimedDispatch, recordDispatch and registerLoop, so a forked skill's row goes through the same completion and logUsage path as a background launch with no second writer.
The per-loop probe set is bounded by STEP_TALLY_CAP and cleared at loop end, matching its docstring, and noticeFork is cheap after the first request (a set lookup).
The turn.step hook keeps the tally ahead of the lookup and every failure is swallowed, honoring the 'no hook throws into a turn' contract.
Tests cover the first-request-only lookup, a resumed fork, a non-harness project, a multi-word description and an unknown loop id.

The Forked skills subsection matches noticeFork in tracker.ts point for point: one lookup per loop, a re-lookup after a resume (probedLoops and loopsAtom are both cleared at loop end), resolveWatch before $.agent.list() so a non-harness project never asks, SKILL-header stripping through unclaimedDispatch, and background-style registration.
The README lists exactly the four context: fork skills that use harness:messenger (c-msg, branch-commit-msg, merge-commit-msg, pr-sum), and its 0.8.0 version marker matches plugin.json.
The roast-my-code dispatch prompt is now a concrete template with SKILL: first, pinned by the new test_roast_dispatch_prompt_names_roast_my_code_first contract test.
The hooks table, the loops state key and the Background usage-figure bullet were updated with the new subsection, so the reference tables do not drift from it.

noticeFork reuses unclaimedDispatch, recordDispatch and registerLoop, so a fork gets the same plugin-prefix stripping, standalone fallback, D8 path filtering and background figures as any unclaimed run, with no parallel row path.
firstProbe is synchronous before any await, bounded by STEP_TALLY_CAP and cleared at loop end, so a loop is looked up once per run of turns and a resumed fork is caught again.

The new tracker tests are behavioral through the fake engine: one lookup per loop, resumed fork, off-form description, outside a harness project and the return-block signal all assert written rows, not stub calls.
The roast prompt keeps `Scope:` and `Intensity:` mixed case, so the leading header block ends after `SKILL:` and a scope path never reaches the row's `fields`.
The README names the engine observation the detection depends on (Claude Code 2.1.318) and both failure modes, instead of pretending the `/<skill>` description is a contract.
The schema description, both manifests, the README hook and state tables and the version bumps move together in one change.

important.name: Once-per-loop lookup test cannot catch the loss of the probe set
important.summary:
The test 'the agent list is asked once per loop, not once per request' steps a loop the list describes as a fork (`fork('loop-f')`). The first step registers loop-f in `loopsAtom` (noticeFork -> registerLoop, tracker.ts:309), so on steps 2 and 3 the `loopsAtom[loopId] !== undefined` guard at tracker.ts:301 already returns before `$.agent.list()`. If `firstProbe`/`probedLoops` (tracker.ts:273-285) were deleted, `asked.calls` would still be 1 and the test would still pass. The probe set only matters for loops that never register: foreground Agent loops and non-fork loops, which the test does not use. It also leaves loop-f in the module-level `probedLoops` and `stepTallies` without ending the loop, so it relies on the harness giving each test fresh plugin module state.

Also (roast): The loopsAtom early return at tracker.ts:301 is never exercised: older background tests register no `agent.list` answer, so deleting the guard changes nothing any test observes. The README limitation (a synchronous Agent dispatch described as `/token` logs two rows) is likewise unpinned, so a fix or regression in either goes unnoticed.
fix: Make the loop one that never registers: `const asked = listing(on, [{ id: 'loop-n', type: 'general-purpose', description: 'Draft the commit message' }])`, then `await steps($, seen, 'loop-n', 1, 2, 3)`, `expect(asked.calls).toBe(1)`, and end it with `await loopEnd($, 'loop-n')` so no probe or tally state is left behind.
Keep the fork case as well, and add a second loop that is not a fork, asserting calls === 2 after three steps on each loop.

Add a test in the 'forked skill usage rows' describe: a background Agent launch whose loop the listing describes as `/harness:c-msg` steps and ends, and exactly one row is logged, under the dispatch's header skill, with `agent.list` asked zero times.
Add a second test for a synchronous dispatch whose loop is listed as `/x`, asserting the two rows the README documents.

important.name: No test covers the guard that keeps a background Agent loop from being logged a second time as a fork
important.summary: noticeFork skips any loop already in `loopsAtom` (tracker.ts:301), which is how a background Agent launch registers its loop (registerLoop after an `async_launched` result). Without that guard, a background loop whose agent-list entry reads `/<skill>` would get a second unclaimed run and a second usage row at its loop end. 'an Agent dispatch loop is not taken for a fork' (tracker.test.ts:719-727) covers only a foreground loop whose description is not a fork, so the description regex rejects it. No test registers `agent.list` next to a background launch, so deleting the `loopsAtom` check would leave every test passing.
fix: Add a test in 'forked skill usage rows': `world(on, () => ({ result: { status: 'async_launched', agentId: 'loop-b', description: 'r', prompt: '', outputFile: 'f', resolvedModel: 'claude-sonnet-5-5' }, text: 'launched' }))`, `const asked = listing(on, [fork('loop-b')])`, `await dispatch($, 'SKILL: todo-edit', 'harness:messenger')`, `await steps($, seen, 'loop-b', 100)`, `await loopEnd($, 'loop-b')`; then expect one usage row with skill 'todo-edit' and `asked.calls` equal to 0.

important.name: roast-my-code prompt no longer ends with the Developer guidance line when code is pasted
important.summary:
The new Step 2 template puts `Developer guidance:` as the fourth line of the fenced block (line 40), then says pasted code follows the block after one blank line (line 45). With pasted code and guidance both present, the prompt ends with the code, not the guidance line. That contradicts the skill's own line 13 (the guidance is carried 'as a final `Developer guidance:` line') and the shared contract in plugins/harness/reference/skill_arguments.md:31 ('Such a prompt ends with one `Developer guidance:` line'). The old prose set no order, so this PR introduces the conflict.

Also (roast): SKILL.md:13 says the dispatch prompt carries the guidance 'as a final `Developer guidance:` line', while SKILL.md:45 puts pasted code after the block. With a snippet scope the guidance line is not the prompt's final line, so the two instructions disagree on where it goes.
fix: Change line 45 to: 'Pasted code goes after the `Intensity:` line, separated by one blank line, verbatim; the `Developer guidance:` line, when present, stays the prompt's last line, after the code.' Then move `Developer guidance:` out of the fenced block (or note that it moves below pasted code). The contract test checks only block[0] and block[1], so it still passes.
Alternatively, keep the block as is and say pasted code goes between the `Intensity:` line and the `Developer guidance:` line, so the guidance line stays last.
Reword SKILL.md:13 to 'as the header block's last line, `Developer guidance:`, and nowhere else'.

minor.name: Known limitation on single-/token Agent descriptions overstates the double row
minor.summary:
Lines 319-320 say any `Agent` call whose `description` is a single `/token` is taken for a fork and logs a second row. In tracker.ts, `noticeFork` (line 301) returns early when the loop is already in `loopsAtom`. A background launch registers its loop from the launch result (`registerLoop`), normally before the loop's first request finishes streaming, so it is usually skipped. The double row comes from a foreground (synchronous) `Agent` call, whose loop is never in `loopsAtom`.

Also (roast): README.md:319-320 says any `Agent` call whose description is a single `/token` is taken for a fork and logs a second row. noticeFork returns early when loopsAtom already holds the loop (tracker.ts:301), and a background launch registers its loop from the async_launched result before its first request ends, so only a synchronous dispatch double-logs. The limitation is real; its scope is wrong.
fix: Reword: 'A foreground `Agent` call whose own `description` is a single `/token` would be taken for a fork as well and log a second row (a background launch is normally registered before its first request ends, and is skipped)'.

Reword README.md:319 to 'A synchronous `Agent` call whose own `description` is a single `/token` would be taken for a fork as well and log a second row; a background launch is registered first and is not.'

minor.name: An Agent dispatch whose description is '/word' is mistaken for a fork and logs twice
minor.summary:
noticeFork decides a loop is a forked skill only from the agent-list description matching /^\/(\S+)$/. The description of an Agent-tool dispatch is free text from the dispatching model, so a one-token description such as '/review' matches too. For a synchronous dispatch the first turn.step fires before the Agent result, so the loop is registered in loopsAtom as a fork, recordLoopEnd then writes a row under that name, and recordResult writes a second row for the same dispatch (one tracked run per path). The test 'an Agent dispatch loop is not taken for a fork' only covers a multi-word description.

Also (runtime): firstProbe marks the loop as probed before resolveWatch and $.agent.list run. If either rejects (the hook swallows it with .catch(noop)) or the agent list does not yet hold the loop on its first request, no later request retries and the forked skill's usage row is never written until the loop ends and is resumed. The docstring promises only 'asked about once per run of turns', but the failure path silently drops the run.

Also (runtime): noticeFork calls recordDispatch, which stores the unclaimed run in runsAtom, and only then registerLoop. If registerLoop (or the second update inside it) throws, the hook's .catch(noop) hides it, the loop is never in loopsAtom, nothing completes the run, and dropUnclaimed never removes it. The Agent path avoids this because recordResult/complete always reaches dropUnclaimed in its finally; the unclaimed-run contract ('once its usage row is attempted the run is dropped, bounding state') does not hold here.

Also (roast): noticeFork resolves the project (resolveWatch: a harness.json read plus the uncached `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`) before it asks the agent list whether the loop is a fork at all. Background launches skip it through the loopsAtom check, but every synchronous Agent subagent is unregistered on its first request, so each one now pays a git spawn, awaited inside the turn.step hook before the request result passes on. The README cost bullet (README.md:315-317) still says only an `Agent` call resolves the project. The probe needs none of the sentinel root it pays for. A fork detector that taxes every non-fork is an odd trade.
fix: Skip noticeFork for loops that an Agent tool.call is currently dispatching, for example by keeping the pending Agent dispatch descriptions or a counter of in-flight Agent calls and comparing before registering.
Accept the collision and state in the FORK_DESCRIPTION comment that a one-token '/word' Agent description is indistinguishable from a fork; add a test pinning the chosen behavior.
Mark the loop probed only after agent.list answered (move the probedLoops add after the list call, or delete the mark in a catch), so a failed lookup is retried on the next request.
Wrap the recordDispatch and registerLoop pair so a failure calls dropUnclaimed($, runId) before rethrowing, or register the loop first and the run second.

Ask the agent list first and call resolveWatch only when forkOf matches, then reword README.md:170 ('Outside a harness project the list is never asked') and the `outside a harness project` test to say the project is resolved only for a fork loop.

Keep the order but document the cost: extend the README.md:315 bullet to say every subagent loop not registered as a background launch also resolves the project, with the uncached git call, on its first request.

minor.name: recordLoopEnd docstring still describes background subagents only
minor.summary: The docstring of recordLoopEnd says 'A background subagent's turn ended' and 'A synchronous agent's loop ends here too and is left to its result'. The function now also completes a forked skill's loop: noticeFork registers that loop in loopsAtom, so this is the only place its usage row is written. The body also clears probedLoops, which the docstring never mentions. A reader of the docstring would not expect a loop no Agent call launched to be handled here.
fix: Reword the docstring to cover 'a registered loop's turn ended: a background subagent or a forked skill (noticeFork)', and note that the loop's probe mark is cleared so a resumed fork is looked up again.

minor.name: Schema top-level description omits forked-skill rows
minor.summary: The top-level description says the file holds one row per returned Agent dispatch and that a generic row takes skill, role, run id, agent id and PR from its prompt's leading header block. The PR adds rows for forked skill loops (noticeFork in tracker.ts), which no Agent call dispatches and which have no prompt header: skill comes from the agent-list description, and every other field falls back. Only the `skill` property description was updated to mention forks, so the intro still reads as if every row comes from an Agent dispatch.
fix: Add a clause to the top-level description at line 5, e.g. 'a forked skill (`context: fork`) loop, which no Agent call dispatches, also writes a generic row, with its skill read from the loop and every other header-derived field at its fallback'.
